data.instructions:
Minor vs Major errors:
Every error span you mark must be assigned one of two severity levels:
Minor:The meaning is essentially preserved. A reader would notice the translation is slightly awkward or imprecise, but would still understand the message correctly. Minor errors include small word choice differences, minor grammar issues, or slight shifts in tone that do not change the core meaning.
Major:The meaning is changed, lost, or seriously misleading. The reader could misunderstand the intent or act on wrong information. Major errors include hallucinated translation, reversed meanings, dropped key information, or incorrect numbers.
Once you detect an error, click on the beginning and end of the span to mark it as a minor or major error. You will have the above short description of minor and major errors during the annotation.
